The Signature Spread

Simple, honest, and unchanged for generations — the food Lahore wakes up for, and stays up for.

The Icon

Siri Paye with Naan

Cow and goat trotters simmered low and slow until the gravy turns rich and silky. Tear into a hot naan, scoop, and eat it the Walled City way — with your hands, at any hour.

Always Brewing

Chai

A strong cup of dhaba chai to cut through the richness of the paye — the pause every meal here ends with, poured fresh around the clock.

The Classic

Lassi

Thick, creamy lassi — the timeless Lahori partner to a heavy plate of paye, especially on a slow morning in the old city.

A Walled City Institution Since 1953

Tucked into Kali Beri Bazar, near Taj Mahal Sweets in Shahi Mohallah, by Taxali Gate, Fazal Din Phajja Siri Paye has been serving Lahore since 1953 — long before food streets and food apps, when a name travelled by word of mouth alone.

Generations have made the trip into the old city for the same bowl: students at dawn, families at lunch, night owls at 3 a.m. The recipe, the bazar, and the welcome have stayed the same.
